title: Customer Collaboration Retreat - Facilitator Runbook
summary: Two-day hands-on collaboration retreat for senior customer stakeholders and Redwood SEs to co-design a production-ready POC and define a deployment decision playbook. Focus areas: workload profiling, latency/cost tradeoffs, routing and fallback policies, and rollout gating criteria.
prework: Customer to provide 3 representative production prompts and expected SLAs
Customer to share current traffic distribution and 1 week of anonymized request traces (CSV)
Redwood SEs to prepare a short performance baseline (hosted vs dedicated) for a similar model family
Participant list and roles confirmed 5 business days before retreat
success_criteria: Agreed POC scope with measurable KPIs (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, error budget)
Deployment decision matrix completed (hosted/dedicated/private) with recommended next step
A prioritized list of engineering tasks and owners for a 6-week POC sprint
At least one validated fallback policy and rollback checklist documented
agenda_items: Day 0 (Pre-meet): 30m alignment call (stakeholder goals, constraints, prework check)
Day 1 - Morning: 60m context and goals; 45m traffic & prompt walkthrough; 30m baseline demo (short)
Day 1 - Afternoon: 90m lab: latency vs cost tradeoff exercises (guided), 45m breakout: routing policies & failure modes
Day 1 - Late: 30m synthesis: define POC success metrics and initial scope
Day 2 - Morning: 60m workshop: deployment decision matrix and security/compliance review, 60m deep dive: caching/batching/quantization impacts
Day 2 - Afternoon: 90m runbook co-authoring: rollout plan, canary strategy, observability checkpoints; 30m ops dry run (incident playbook)
Day 2 - Close: 45m prioritization, owners, timeline, and next steps; 15m feedback + retrospective

facilitation_notes: Timing and tone: keep sessions highly interactive; alternate 20–30m demos with hands-on labs. Use visible timers and a dedicated scribe. For breakout groups, assign one customer engineer + one Redwood SE. Prepare two lab environments: (A) cost-optimized config and (B) low-latency config. If we run out of time on technical deep dives, prioritize producing the decision matrix and runbook drafts. Parking lot: keep a running Google Doc for follow-ups. Encourage explicit decision signals: green/yellow/red on each matrix criterion. Communication protocols: during incident-playbook dry run, walk through the alert->escalation->fallback timeline in role-play. Escalation path draft: SE lead -> Customer infra lead -> Redwood SRE -> Product PM. Accessibility: provide slide PDF and a one-page cheat sheet summarizing SLA targets. Logistics checklist: whiteboard, HDMI, 2 laptops with SSH keys provisioned, access to sample trace files, Slack channel #retreat-<customer-shortname>. Remote participants: use breakout rooms and a shared Collab doc; ensure video is on for facilitators. Post-retreat artifacts: baseline benchmark CSVs, finished decision matrix, draft runbook, prioritized task list, retrospective notes. Quote to remind facilitators: 'Decisions > Perfection' — push for pragmatic agreement on next steps rather than exhaustive investigation.
required_artifacts: Model family variants and sizes list
Access to customer's dev/staging endpoints (read-only) if available
Prebuilt baseline performance report from Redwood SEs
